# Repos that release.yml's notify-downstream repository_dispatches `upstream-release`
# {tag, version, sha} to on a busbar release. Each repo has its own release-on-upstream
# workflow (plus a daily-cron fallback) that re-pins to `sha`, bumps its own version, and
# publishes. One line per downstream repo.
#
# GetBusbar/marketing IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT, AND ITS ABSENCE IS THE DECISION, NOT AN OVERSIGHT.
# The marketing site's deploy must not be a dependency of the release (owner, 2026-09-06). It was
# on this list, so every release RAN the site deploy: `notify-downstream` fails outright if any
# single dispatch fails, and `consumer-verification` hangs off it -- so a marketing-side token,
# rename or outage could turn a perfectly good, already-published busbar release red, and a
# release could be held up by a site that ships nothing users execute. The site keeps its OWN
# trigger (its push-to-main deploy plus its daily poll of busbar's /releases/latest), which is
# what makes it self-healing without being wired into this path. Nothing in this repository
# triggers, waits on, or `needs:` the site deploy.
#
# The site's state is still OBSERVED, never depended on: verify-deploy.yml's checks (g)/P6/(k)/(n)
# read getbusbar.com AFTER publication, and cannot gate it -- they run in `consumer-verification`,
# which is downstream of an already-public release by construction.
